title: PR context map and annotated rationale (scratchpad)
content:
Quick goals for this scratchpad:
- Capture the mental model I want reviewers to leave the PR with: what user-facing behavior changed, why the change was made, where to look in the codebase for the hot paths, and which tests/migrations need follow-up.
- Produce a compact "context map" that can be pasted at the top of a PR description and used as a reviewer checklist.

Why this helps: when PRs are large / cross-cutting, reviewers waste time chasing down intent. Anchoring the diff to concrete behaviors + ownership boundaries reduces back-and-forth and makes rollbacks/fallbacks clearer.

Draft context map structure (for PR descriptions):
1) One-line user-impact summary (what changes from the user/app viewpoint)
2) Three bullet reasons for the change (performance, correctness, UX, policy)
3) Components touched and brief responsibilities (service A: cache; runtime: kv-cache; ui: toggle)
4) Risk surface and immediate mitigations (e.g., fallbacks, feature flag, canary region)
5) Quick test plan (unit + integration + smoke + perf)
6) Follow-ups (migration scripts, metrics dashboards, cleanup tasks)

Example (mock PR):
1) One-line: "Decrease inference tail latency for short prompts by enabling KV prefix-merge for small sequences."
2) Reasons:
   - Long request spikes showed high GPU kernel overhead for repeated short prompts (see INF-2483).
   - Existing prefix caching invalidation semantics caused frequent misses for multi-turn chat.
   - This preserves output quality while reducing cost by batching more effectively.
3) Components touched:
   - serving-runtime/kv_cache: new prefix-merge logic (owner: @samir)
   - platform-routing: fallback policy updates (owner: @rae)
   - tests/legacy: updated replay tests to include multi-turn sequences (owner: @inez)
4) Risk surface + mitigations:
   - Risk: cache correctness for variable-length keys -> added property-based tests + canary flag rollout to 5% customers for 48h.
   - Mitigation: automatic fallback to legacy code path on mismatch detected (logs metric: kv_merge_mismatch).
5) Quick test plan:
   - Unit: Add key collision tests + new prefix-match fuzz harness.
   - Integration: End-to-end smoke with 1k synthetic chat sessions.
   - Perf: Microbench on p3/dedicated to confirm median and 95th p99 improvement.
6) Follow-ups:
   - INF-2483: add dashboard tile for kv_merge_hit_rate and kv_merge_mismatch (owner: analytics)
   - Remove feature flag after 4 weeks and when error rate below threshold (owner: release)
   - Clean up deprecated TTL-based invalidation code in 6 weeks (tech debt)

Reviewer checklist (paste into PR):
- [ ] I can rephrase the one-line user impact in my own words.
- [ ] The three reasons make sense and are mutually consistent.
- [ ] I understand which files are the hot path for production (list in code comments).
- [ ] The tests added address both correctness and the common failure modes.
- [ ] There are clear rollback/fallback steps and metrics to alert on.
- [ ] Security and privacy considerations covered (no leakage via cache keys).
- [ ] Performance expectations are documented with test commands and infra.

Refactor idea bucket (things seen while walking diffs):
- Split large kv_cache.c into two logical modules: matcher (prefix logic) and storage (eviction + serialization). Currently the file mixes matching heuristics with storage mechanics which makes reasoning in reviews hard.
- Introduce a small adapter interface around routing policies so runtime changes don't require edits in platform routing module; makes canarying easier.
- Reduce cognitive load by adding short header doc comments (2-3 lines) at top of every core module that say: "purpose, invariants, common failure modes."

Follow-up task seeds (for issues/todos):
- Create INF-xxxx for migrating replay tests to new harness (owner: QA)
- Perf regression alert rule: kv_merge_latency increase > 15% for 5 min (owner: SRE)
- Mini-postmortem template if canary triggers fallback within first 24h (owner: release)

Open questions / discussion items to put in PR comments:
- Is prefix-merge semantically safe under eventual consistency with cross-region replication? If not, we need a per-region keyspace or a stronger invalidation step.
- How does this interact with quantized model variants that have different tokenization edge cases? Should tokenization be normalized at the cache key layer?
- Should the feature flag be customer-level or route-level? Route-level gives finer control but adds complexity to rollout tooling.

Notes to self (rough):
- When writing the PR, include short code pointers to areas reviewers should inspect: kv_cache/matcher.go:line 120-220, runtime/kv_client.py:call site, tests/replay/fixtures/chat_small.json
- Keep the PR title short + include subsystem tags in brackets: "[kv-cache][runtime] prefix-merge + tests"
- Consider attaching a 60s demo gif in PR to show perf delta on local env.

Why this format might be useful across other PRs:
- It's portable: same six-section map fits bugfix, refactor, and feature PRs.
- Forces author to think about rollback and metrics early.
- Helps reviewers switch from line-level nitpicks to risk/impact conversations when appropriate.

End of scratchpad. Will refine and convert into a PR template snippet once I test it on an internal small change.

Random links and references I used while drafting:
- Linear issue INF-2483 (spike notes)
- Internal perf run: https://internal-perf/reports/kv-prefix-2025-11-01
- Example PR to copy context-map placement: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4489
